file_name: Semaan et al. - 2023 - Tackling the COVID 19 infodemic among Syrian refugees in Lebanon Development and evaluation of the W.txt

barriers.description: COVID-19 curfews and lockdown restrictions limited the research team's ability to visit target areas and conduct in-person engagement with beneficiaries.
barriers.justification: This external policy constraint directly hindered designers' ability to manage user understanding, facilitate user involvement, and study the context of use through face-to-face fieldwork and observation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: working with Syrian refugees in urban areas has been even more challenging due to the restrictions imposed by COVID-19 curfews and lockdowns, which limited the opportunity to visit the targeted areas and talk to our intended beneficiaries.

barriers.description: Refugees' avoidance of registration with authorities (due to fear of discrimination or deportation) made recruitment and access to the target population difficult.
barriers.justification: This trust and safety issue impeded facilitation of user involvement and constrained the team's ability to gain comprehensive, diverse user understanding and engage users as co-designers.
barriers.reference_excerpt: working with a very mobile and hard-to-reach population (i.e., Syrian refugees living in urban settings) has always been challenging. These refugees avoid being registered with the UNHCR or local municipalities to avoid discrimination or the risk of being deported to Syria.

barriers.description: Platform technical limits (closed WhatsApp group maximum size) constrained the project's ability to scale outreach without substantial human resources.
barriers.justification: This operational constraint limited the designers' ability to facilitate wide user involvement, evaluate the intervention at scale, and plan scalable deployment strategies.
barriers.reference_excerpt: A technical limitation that needs to be considered is the maximum number of users allowed in a closed WhatsApp group. While WhatsApp has recently increased this number from 512 to 1,024, it still limits the reach of WhatsApp-based communication interventions targeting larger groups... scaling this up would require human resources to manage these groups.

barriers.description: Interactive/chatbot features could not be added because they require WhatsApp Business API access and additional funding, preventing bidirectional interaction.
barriers.justification: This limitation blocked integrating user feedback and iteration through interactive channels, reducing the team's capacity to support ongoing dialogic engagement and refine the service based on real-time user queries.
barriers.reference_excerpt: Only one participant disliked the fact that it was impossible to interact with the service and to ask questions... these are features available in the WhatsApp for Business, not for closed user groups. Therefore, we considered transforming the service into an open group service, but more funding would be needed for such development.

barriers.description: The sample was limited to participants from one suburb recruited via partner organizations, reducing diversity and generalizability of user insights.
barriers.justification: This sampling and recruitment limitation constrained designers' ability to manage user understanding across the broader refugee population and to study varied contexts of use necessary for robust requirement specification and evaluation.
barriers.reference_excerpt: First, the users who participated in this project were from one suburb of the capital city. They were highly interested in contributing to the project so that they might have different views and experiences than refugees living in smaller urban areas.

barriers.description: Interviews were not recorded and student researchers combined notes and summarized findings without formal coding, limiting qualitative analysis rigor.
barriers.justification: This methodological practice reduced the team's capacity to deeply analyze and synthesize user insights, hindering management of user understanding, specification of user requirements, and robust evaluation of the design.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The interviews were not recorded, and students took notes without collecting personal identifiers. All four students combined their notes to summarize findings and organize them without coding around the themes...
